sources.title: Structured interview source containing the RandomSet prompt
Deterministic and randomized RandomSet differential validation

claims.text: The preserved source asks for a RandomSet with set/remove/contains/randomGet described as O(1), without defining duplicate insertion, empty randomGet, language, concurrency, or worst-case versus expected/amortized complexity semantics.
The candidate uses a dense ArrayList plus a value-to-index HashMap and swap-with-last deletion, maintaining values.size()==index.size() and index.get(values.get(i))==i.

The reproducible Java validation checks duplicate insertion, removal, contains, empty randomGet, swap deletion and 100000 seeded randomized operations against an independent HashSet membership oracle while repeatedly checking the internal index bijection.

The candidate explicitly distinguishes the classic expected/amortized constant-time Java-container analysis from a strict deterministic worst-case O(1) guarantee, which the source wording alone does not define sufficiently.
